world_poi_layout.intent: Use the ten report-backed world-kit families as a constrained construction vocabulary for generators that compose believable POIs and battlefield layouts; do not scatter or register the source pieces as a direct asset dump.
generationTargets: modular kit grammar with compatible sockets, scale, style, and condition rules
macro-to-micro composition rules for settlements, industry, outposts, derelicts, and landmarks
connected road, service, pedestrian, assault, naval, amphibious, and resource-access networks
planet- and region-specific POI identity rather than generic repeated settlements
seeded structural variation and believable world dressing without blocking gameplay
requiredGeneratorOutputs: hierarchical POI plans with stable IDs and exact site-class intent
validated access graphs connecting entrances, roads, services, resources, and tactical routes
district and parcel composition before decorative placement
bounded deterministic variation that avoids repetition and preserves regional identity
world dressing constrained by traversal, buildability, sightlines, hazards, and economy clearance
world_poi_layout.promotionBoundary: World-kit grammar and generated layouts remain offline candidates until numeric, visual, traversal, deterministic, recovery, phone, and explicit runtime-registration gates pass.

world_maritime_seaplatform.candidateMappingGap: Exact source IDs and hashes for any additional user-provided floating-platform model-pack pieces are not yet mapped. Do not invent an mf-seaplatform-v1 family or reinterpret prompt-site IDs as shipped modules.

derivationNotes: All 48 canonical campaign maps are Stage 10 preparation targets. The six existing FULL_V1 maps are baseline-preserving improvement targets, not exclusions.

The 334-module report-backed world-kit subset is a tools/generator library: its 327 eligible pieces form modular grammar and composition inputs for believable POI and world layouts, not a direct asset dump.

maps[].processingAssetFamilies refers only to worldKitFamilies and means source-level world-layout study and candidate preparation. It does not grant ship, section, decal, character, export, registration, or runtime authority.

Brood maps require an organic conversion asset family that is not present in the hard-surface pack; ruined hard-surface modules are substrate only.
Pyraeth and Nordhall can use neutral/brutalist modules as structural proxies, but faction-specific pressure/heat and machine/glacial treatments remain authoring gaps.

Current world-kit reports are dirty local evidence. The 2026-08-28 handoff records the pre-repair failure state; the current building report was rebuilt after the numeric repair. Re-hash and re-run gates before promotion.

The UGA interior decal contract explicitly forbids exterior-hull binding. Exterior hull livery remains a separate unapproved authoring lane.

topologyReferenceContract.canonicalScopeEffect: None. The references guide future exact-plan and generator work; they do not add maps, replace canonical art, or automatically expand the current 48-map campaign catalogue.

scaleLadder.designRule: One dominant objective, short rotations, two readable primary approaches, and a limited flank or amphibious bypass.
Multiple crossings and resource pockets, a contested center, and at least one route whose risk changes with the biome hazard.
Several fronts, distributed colonies or derelicts, layered primary/flank/water routes, and two strategic anchors where appropriate.
Long-duration team warfare with route tiers, regional logistics, multiple objectives, protected and exposed resource bands, and no single mandatory choke.

primary, flank, naval, amphibious, service, and evacuation connectivity
bridge, causeway, gate, tunnel, rail, and destructible-route state
objective, colony, derelict, resource, and hazard hierarchy
elevation, visibility, buildability, traversal, and economy clearance
deterministic hazard timing and route-state recovery

grammar: lava fissures and seas divide fronts
bridges, forge passes, coolant or geothermal routes, and elevated crowns control rotation
eruption, vent, ash, and magma events alter route risk without hiding required connectivity
islands, mainland shelves, naval lanes, and amphibious landings create cross-domain fronts
bridges and causeways are logistics gates rather than decorative links
meltable ice crossings require explicit open, weakened, destroyed, and recovered traversal states
toxic channels and living terrain split land movement while supporting amphibious bypasses
spore weather changes visibility and exposure, and fungus canopies create ambush or elevation pockets
colony-growth hubs, hive cores, and heartroot objectives spread influence through the route graph
Brood treatment consumes and infests structural substrate; it does not become a selectable civic building style
crystal ridges and elevated plateaus create vision and artillery control
destructible crystal barriers open alternate paths
luminous water routes, bridges, colonies, and a central citadel or crown create layered contests
storm cycles change visibility, sea state, landing safety, and route exposure
ports, sea gates, headlands, islands, and coastal fortifications connect naval logistics to land fronts
tides and amphibious landings create timed bypasses without invalidating spawn access
river confluences, shallow channels, boardwalks, and bridge networks define movement
mangrove canopy and reeds reduce sightlines while marsh attrition, bog gas, deep mud, and sinkholes punish overextension
colonies and resources need redundant supply access across water and land
pressure domes, drowned colonies, reefs, escarpments, and broken causeways create protected and exposed shelves
hydrothermal vent cycles, deep trenches, and drop-offs create timed hazard zones
water routes and amphibious drops must connect across vertical plateaus without bypassing every choke
pillars, cave bridges, chasms, sinkholes, and unstable ledges make vertical control part of the route graph
underground rivers support naval and amphibious flanks while tunnels enable stealth rotation
subterranean rail and logistics links connect arcologies, mining complexes, colonies, and objectives

futureContract.buildOrder: Validate scale, spawn zones, route and transition graph, water/depth/layer semantics, objectives, hazards, resources, and named district/site plots before placing structures or dressing.
futureContract.cacheIdentityRule: Include topology schema version and semantic/layout hash in the world-topology cache key before any new route domain or dynamic topology state is enabled.

battlefieldTopologyImplementationBoundar.massiveReferenceRule: The 6v6/8v8 massive sheets are topology references only. maritimeSeaplatformProcessingGate.classificationRule: A sea platform is a world/maritime POI with stable gameplay deck and water-space contracts. It is neither an ordinary terrain-backed building nor a SHIP_SECTION asset.

supportModes.fixed_caisson: Support geometry reaches the declared seabed datum and remains static.
supportModes.floating_pontoon: Visible flotation and mooring carry the platform at the declared waterline.
supportModes.semi_submersible: Authored ballast states control draft and freeboard without changing route identity implicitly.
supportModes.shoreline_quay: A fixed shore interface or revetment, not a floating structure.
supportModes.sea_link: Causeway, gangway, or bridge joining declared deck, shore, or platform sockets.
supportModes.sea_wreck: Afloat or sunk destroyed state with explicit naval and deck-navigation effects.

maritimeSeaplatformProcessingGate.mappingRule: Record exact source IDs, source hashes, and exactly one primary support mode for each candidate. Do not infer floating eligibility from platform, dock, deck, hull, or landing-deck names and do not double-count a module already present in a world-kit family.
requiredDatums: mooring, anchoring, seabed-support, or authored stabilization model
accessContracts: naval clearance envelope around hull and supports
vehicle-capable ramps, bridges, elevators, or causeways where required
at least two viable approaches for major combat platforms
no support column, decoration, or mooring line may silently block a declared route
navigationAndCollision: stable deck nav/build proxy independent from render mesh
simple water-domain hull obstacle and support collision
separate land, naval, amphibious, and transition-node semantics
wave animation must not move gameplay collision or route anchors
no false walkable overhangs, submerged obstacles, or visual gaps that disagree with clearance
environmentGates: shore, causeway, dock, and bridge connection tolerances
seabed depth or anchor feasibility where relevant
maritimeSeaplatformProcessingGate.supportModeGate: A fixed platform must visibly and geometrically reach its seabed supports. A floating platform must visibly demonstrate flotation and mooring. A semi-submersible must declare deterministic ballast states. A shoreline quay must connect to a valid shore datum.
maritimeSeaplatformProcessingGate.destructionRule: Every stage has a deterministic deck, naval-clearance, access, objective, and collision transition. Sinking or collapse uses a bounded wreck/rubble footprint and may not strand units or create an unplanned total route lock.
currentRuntimeGaps: water buildings render at a fixed water-plane height and have no structural buoyancy or wave response
building destruction currently uses generic collapse, crater, deformation, rubble, and wreck behavior without a water-specific sinking branch
performanceGates: LOD0 through strategic LOD or HLOD
shared maritime materials and trim sheets
bounded draw calls and water-effect cost
hardware-GPU phone captures at tactical and strategic zoom
maritimeSeaplatformProcessingGate.promotionBoundary: No sea-platform candidate is runtime-ready until exact source mapping, human visual review, route-domain validation, destruction-state validation, phone performance, and explicit registration pass.

brutalistMegacity3DGenerationContract.purpose: Generate a modular, optimized, fully playable brutalist science-fiction military-industrial RTS district rather than a dense cinematic city or generic skyscraper field.
macroHierarchy: central command citadel or fortress anchor
inner governmental, military, and industrial ring
middle factory, barracks, reactor, depot, logistics, and worker districts
outer defense, wall, yard, storage, ruin, and infrastructure districts
fortified perimeter with several controlled entrances

assemblyHierarchy.rule: Do not scale a site assembler into a megacity by increasing asset density.
order: reserve primary, secondary, flank, naval, service, objective, hazard, and destruction-transition corridors
instantiate bounded deterministic site blueprints inside those plots
place gameplay collision and traversal proxies

combatSpaceArchetypes: bounded industrial grid with multiple vehicle lanes
brutalistMegacity3DGenerationContract.chokepointRule: Use intentional fortress gates, bridges, industrial corridors, tunnels, wall breaches, elevated causeways, and reactor passages. Every major choke needs a nearby alternate route or destructible state so a front cannot become permanently blocked.

districtIdentities.logistics: vehicle depots, warehouses, and transport infrastructure
districtIdentities.ruined: damaged buildings and collapsed infrastructure with controlled traversal states

laneDefinitions.modular-kit-grammar: Define compatible module sockets, scale bands, style and condition transitions, repetition limits, and legal adjacency so generators assemble structures and terrain intentionally.
laneDefinitions.poi-composition-rules: Generate settlement, industrial, derelict, outpost, and landmark POIs from hierarchical district, parcel, frontage, service, defense, and landmark rules rather than loose asset scattering.
laneDefinitions.road-access-connectivity: Build and validate connected road, pedestrian, service, assault, resource, and evacuation graphs from each POI entrance to the wider battlefield.
laneDefinitions.world-dressing-variation: Apply deterministic regional variation, occupancy history, wear, utility props, vegetation or infestation, and restrained clutter while preserving traversal, buildability, sightlines, and economy clearance.
laneDefinitions.planet-region-identity: Drive generator palette, composition, skyline, infrastructure, condition, and dressing rules from planet, faction, and region identity so each region is visually and tactically distinct.
laneDefinitions.macro-map-composition: Generate terrain masses, landmark silhouettes, safe build basins, POI hierarchy, and approach structure before parcel, module, or dressing placement.
laneDefinitions.traversal-and-chokes: Design primary, secondary, and flanking routes for infantry, small vehicles, and mechs; validate corner cuts, water crossings, and their connection to the road/access graph.
laneDefinitions.resource-expansion-spacing: Place economy expansions against travel time, defensibility, sightlines, and site footprints rather than decorative symmetry.
laneDefinitions.colony-city-districts: Separate colony/city neighborhoods into civic, residential, industrial, defense, and service districts with readable streets.
laneDefinitions.industrial-logistics: Connect refineries, foundries, yards, tanks, gantries, and service corridors without blocking tactical routes.
laneDefinitions.bases-outposts-defense: Give bases and outposts perimeter logic, gates, fallback positions, patrol lanes, and clear assault approaches.
laneDefinitions.derelict-ruin-relic: Use intact-to-ruined states, salvage paths, and landmark relics to tell occupation history without contaminating navigation.
laneDefinitions.spaceport-aprons: Reserve broad landing/apron clearances, approach corridors, cargo staging, and defensible service edges.
laneDefinitions.pressure-dome-subsurface: Link domes and buried facilities through pressure-safe passages, exposed service trenches, and above/below-ground landmarks.
laneDefinitions.waterfront-naval: Coordinate shorelines, sea walls, docks, bridges, naval lanes, and land-to-water economy transitions.
laneDefinitions.hazard-legibility: Make hazard sources, affected routes, shelters, and recovery areas readable at command and tactical zoom.
laneDefinitions.brood-conversion: Treat hard-surface assets only as consumed substrate; add organic route conversion, cocoons, buttresses, hatcheries, and nest channels.
laneDefinitions.compact-map-legibility: Limit landmark count and route branching so the compact theatre remains readable and spawn-safe.
laneDefinitions.large-map-landmark-hierarchy: Use regional anchors and route tiers so large theatres do not become repeated modules or empty travel.
laneDefinitions.full-v1-regression-preservation: Improve the map only with the existing exact requests, stable IDs, topology, determinism, traversal, recovery, and visual baseline preserved or deliberately versioned.
